page: Amazon Web Services c5n.metal is a bare-metal, compute-optimized server powered by Intel Xeon 8124M processors. It features 36 physical cores and 72 vCPUs operating at a clock speed of 3.4 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The system is equipped with 192.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, providing 2.67 GB of RAM per core. This server does not include local storage or dedicated GPUs, relying instead on network-attached storage and boasting a high baseline network bandwidth of 100 Gbps.

In benchmark evaluations, the c5n.metal demonstrates strong multi-core performance, as evidenced by its stress-ng multi-core CPU score of 67384.33 and a PassMark CPU score of 50868.09. Memory performance is highly competitive, with read-only cached small block bandwidth reaching 3741.32 GB/sec and uncached large block read bandwidth at 212.97 GB/sec. Software compilation tasks perform well, with a Geekbench Clang compilation score of 39606.0. However, single-core performance and text generation for large language models are relatively weak, with LLM text generation for a medium 7B model scoring in the bottom 10% at 6.09 tokens per second.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the bare-metal architecture eliminates hypervisor overhead, maximizing the return on compute resources for highly parallelized workloads. The high network throughput of 100 Gbps makes it highly suitable for network-bound applications, distributed databases, and high-performance computing tasks. Given the strong multi-core and database benchmark results, this server is well-suited for intensive database operations, software build pipelines, and parallel scientific simulations, though it is less optimal for GPU-dependent machine learning or single-threaded tasks.
